axes.brief:
Competitive direct elections and defined impeachment coexist with elite coalitions, unequal political resources and military administrative influence.
Focused six-question reassessment: Emergency regulations require legislative approval and the president has a personal electoral mandate. Constitutional succession differs from party-only replacement; there is no general signature-triggered national legislative referendum route.
axes.counterEvidence:
Actual August2026 constitutional review invalidated government-insult provisions; neither broad coalitions nor military influence establish lawful unilateral executive or military replacement.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Emergency regulations require legislative approval and the president has a personal electoral mandate. Constitutional succession differs from party-only replacement; there is no general signature-triggered national legislative referendum route.

answers.rationale: The Constitution provides direct competitive presidential elections and a five-year term renewable once;2024 election selected the current president.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: Competitive direct elections and defined impeachment coexist with elite coalitions, unequal political resources and military administrative influence. Focused interpretation: Emergency regulations require legislative approval and the president has a personal electoral mandate. Constitutional succession differs from party-only replacement; there is no general signature-triggered national legislative referendum route. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Adult voting is not qualified by education or intelligence. Registration and implementation obstacles qualify universality; every current disenfranchisement exception was not retrieved.

National identity-document and communications-control institutions support qualified authority. Current court corrections and retained security restrictions compete on prompt review and ordinary search, producing substantive mixed responses. Regulated civil organisations supply a permission-oriented tendency, but notification and legal-entity registration must not be treated automatically as licensing.
